texts.value: Structural constituent of cytoplasmic lattices, which plays a key role in early embryonic development (PubMed:37922900, PubMed:41772195). Cytoplasmic lattices consist in fibrous structures found in the cytoplasm of oocytes and preimplantation embryos: they are required to store maternal proteins critical for embryonic development, such as ribosomal proteins, cytoskeletal tubulins and proteins controlling epigenetic reprogramming of the preimplantation embryo, in a poised but restrained state, regulating their availability for early embryonic development (PubMed:37922900, PubMed:41772195). Cytoplasmic lattices also tightly control ubiquitination during the oocyte-to-embryo transition by trapping E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase UHRF1 in a compact autoinhibited conformation and maintaining SCF ubiquitin ligase complexes inactive (PubMed:41772195). PADI6 oligomers acts as an essential structural scaffolding element of cytoplasmic lattices (By similarity). In contrast to other members of the family, does not show protein-arginine deiminase activity due to its inability to bind Ca(2+) (PubMed:38656308, PubMed:39286527)
